lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Add a brief target-role identifier or summary near the top.
items.because: A recruiter currently has to infer whether you are pursuing software, ML, or agent-systems roles.

items.says: Replace the example.com contact details if they are placeholders.
items.because: The email and portfolio link should work when you submit the résumé.

items.says: Update “Expected Jun 2026” if you have graduated by the time you apply.
items.because: The degree and date should reflect your completed status.

items.says: Move Mobility Systems Company above Eastern Robotics Co.
items.because: Its May 2025 end date is more recent, and reverse-chronological order makes it easier to find.

items.says: Consider leading with the ML internship for ML or agent roles.
items.because: Its diagnostics, model, inference, and GRPO work is more directly aligned with those roles.

items.says: Clarify which system or incident population the monitoring result covers.
items.because: That context helps a reader judge the result’s scale and relevance.

items.says: Clarify the workload and environment behind the p95 comparison.
items.because: The latency figures should be apples-to-apples.

items.says: “Maintained” and “adds” have mismatched tenses.
Give the release-cycle baseline before it shortened to 3 days.
items.because: The reader cannot tell the size of the improvement.

items.says: Reduce the number of accomplishments competing in one bullet.
items.because: It combines a migration, library rewrite, mentoring, on-call responsibility, and an operational result.

items.says: Clarify the starting point or measurement of the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: That would distinguish sustained improvement from a short-term fluctuation.

items.says: Describe the 71% to 79% accuracy change as an 8-percentage-point increase.
items.because: That states the change precisely.

items.says: Clarify the held-out split and “validated tool-use trajectories.”
items.because: Those details matter to a technical reviewer.

items.says: Add inference hardware, workload, or throughput-trade-off context.
items.because: It would make the latency result more informative for ML-systems roles.

items.says: Clarify how the grouped rollouts relate to the next bullet’s one scored trajectory per prompt.
items.because: The descriptions can sound contradictory given GRPO’s association with multiple rollouts.

items.says: Identify what the 5% latency change measures and its comparison baseline.
Clarify what “one per prompt” means relative to the grouped rollouts.
items.because: The current GRPO descriptions can sound contradictory.

items.says: Substantiate or narrow the claim that training was “stabilised.”
items.because: The implementation detail alone does not show what instability occurred or how improvement was assessed.

items.says: Specify your role in creating or validating the runbook rules.
items.because: Your ownership of the adopted rules may not be clear.

items.says: Replace the broad impact claim with evidence or remove it.
items.because: “Drove adoption” and “improving outcomes” lack a concrete measure or example and read as generic promotion.

items.says: The drop from 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: An alert technical reader may notice the incorrect calculation.

items.says: The change from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not a 12% relative increase.
Add benchmark and evaluation-condition context.
items.because: The reader needs it to interpret the task-completion result.

items.says: Clarify whether you implemented the metrics, proposed them, or both.
items.because: Your contribution should be clear.

items.says: Clarify what “default benchmark” and “every release” mean in practice.
Explain the Kendall correlation result and what was compared.
items.because: “400+ report-level trials” does not by itself explain the evaluation result.

items.says: Distinguish what you personally changed from what maintainers fixed.
items.because: That makes your contribution easier to assess and defend.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific.
items.because: It is a broad capability rather than a named tool or method.

items.says: Broaden the brief skills section with relevant, supportable systems skills.
items.because: It does not yet represent the deployment, testing, infrastructure, and model-serving work described in the experience section.

items.says: Group related skills so the section is easier to scan.
items.because: The current short list does not show the breadth of the systems work.
